correctness.rationale: Two identical additive agents reduce maximum pairwise envy at step t to |d_t|. Since each item of weight w_t changes d by +/-w_t, sum of w_t<=|d_{t-1}|+|d_t| implies C>=ceil((a+2b)/2). When a>=1, release one unit to get |d|=1, let each of b double items flip the sign at cost 1, and pair or cancel remaining units; this attains b+ceil(a/2), including all parity boundaries. At a=0 every odd step gap is at least 2, giving 2ceil(b/2). Under unit-first greedy gaps alternate (1,0) on unit steps and (1,1) versus (2,0) on double steps, so the sole additive-one failure is a positive even number of units and odd b. This is an unrestricted constructive proof, not merely the 529-case finite dynamic program.
